extracted.intended_audience: readers of entertainment news / film and celebrity culture followers
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for assessing comedy (and its relation to drama) in film performances and publicity contexts, as discussed in an entertainment news piece about Ryan Reynolds defending comedy. Emphasizes craftsmanship, emotional grounding, and contextual/ethical considerations around casting and publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy should look and feel effortless
rubrics_metrics.description: "Comedy is also very difficult. But has an added dimension in that it's meant to look and feel effortless. You intentionally hide the stitching and unstitching."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reynolds' point: effective comedy conceals the work behind it so that it appears natural and unforced. Example/anti-pattern: Visible construction or hammy technique undermines the comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hide the 'stitches' (avoid visible mechanics)
rubrics_metrics.description: "You intentionally hide the stitching and unstitching."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: avoid draws of self-conscious or overtly constructed jokes that reveal how the gag is made. The article cites Deadpool & Wolverine as having "stitches" so visible that critics focused on broken canon — showing visible 'stitching' invites scrutiny and can reduce enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy and drama both subsist on tension
rubrics_metrics.description: "Comedy and drama subsist on tension. Both thrive when subverting expectation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats tension and surprise as shared mechanics across genres; good work in either mode manages audience expectations and uses subversion effectively. Use emotional stakes to make subversion meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Both genres should be backstopped by real emotion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when aiming for laughs or tragedy, performances should be grounded in authentic feeling so the stakes matter. This is offered as a commonality that strengthens both comedy and drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptual effectiveness: performances should not 'feel difficult' to the viewer
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer's evaluation: Garfield’s performance is effective because it "doesn't feel difficult at all."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for assessing dramatic performance: invisibility of effort contributes to emotional impact. Contrast with performances where effort or construction is too apparent, which can lessen audience engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparisons between genres/performances are subjective
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that taste and personal perspective shape judgments (e.g., someone preferring Anchorman vs another preferring Melancholia). Use humility when ranking cross-genre work and recognize differing aesthetic values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider ethical/contextual factors in lineup/casting decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The article notes Reynolds' presence highlighted the "absence of Sebastian Stan," reportedly shut out because other actors' teams did not want clients to discuss his Trump biopic, The Apprentice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond craft, lineup and pairing choices carry political and ethical dimensions; evaluators and programmers should be aware that behind-the-scenes decisions (blacklisting, reputational concerns) affect whose voices are heard. The piece flags the broader value: "there's nothing funny about the threat of artists losing the freedom to criticize authority."
